    // The union of two spatial volumes: inside either one.
    Union(a: FunctionVolume3D, b: FunctionVolume3D): FunctionVolume3D
        => FunctionVolume3D(p => a.Eval(p) || b.Eval(p));

    // The intersection of two spatial volumes: inside both.
    Intersection(a: FunctionVolume3D, b: FunctionVolume3D): FunctionVolume3D
        => FunctionVolume3D(p => a.Eval(p) && b.Eval(p));

    // The first volume with the second removed: inside a and not inside b.
    Difference(a: FunctionVolume3D, b: FunctionVolume3D): FunctionVolume3D
        => FunctionVolume3D(p => a.Eval(p) && b.Eval(p).Not);

    // Everything outside the volume.
    Complement(self: FunctionVolume3D): FunctionVolume3D
        => FunctionVolume3D(p => self.Eval(p).Not);

    //==
    // # Concrete shapes as signed distance fields
    //
    // The bridge from the boundary-representation geometry types to the implicit
    // ones: a shape becomes the field reporting the distance to it, after which the
    // whole implicit surface — CSG, smoothing, offsetting, ray marching, sampling
    // onto a lattice — applies to it. Explicit `ToSdf` and never an implicit
    // conversion, because the field cannot recover the shape it came from
    // (Convention: see CONVENTIONS.md - Conversions).
    //
    // These bodies hold the lambda that the primitive bodies in
    // `implicit-sdf.library.plato` deliberately do not: each `ToSdf` closes over its
    // shape and defers to the matching closed-form primitive, which is what keeps
    // the primitives portable and the placement in one place. Fidelity follows from
    // that: every field here is EXACT (`implicit-sdf.concepts.plato`), except the
    // quad patch in space, which is exact only while its four corners are coplanar
    // and not a bound at all once they are not.
    //
    // Read the doc comment for what the sign means, because it differs by shape:
    //
    //  - A SOLID (sphere, disk, capsule, triangle in the plane) gives a true signed
    //    field: negative inside, zero on the boundary, positive outside.
    //  - An unbounded HALF-REGION (a plane, a half-space, a half-plane) gives the
    //    signed field of the region behind its boundary.
    //  - A ZERO-THICKNESS shape (a segment; a triangle or quad patch in space) has
    //    no interior for a sign to describe, so its field is non-negative everywhere
    //    and zero only on the shape itself. It is still a usable distance field —
    //    ray marching and offsetting work — but `IsInside` is false everywhere, and
    //    a Boolean subtraction against it removes nothing. Use the overload taking a
    //    radius or a thickness to get the solid form instead, which is the shape's
    //    Minkowski sum with a ball and has an exact signed distance.

    // The distance to the sphere's surface: negative inside the ball.
    ToSdf(s: Sphere): FunctionSdf3D
        => FunctionSdf3D(p => s.Center.Between(p).Magnitude - s.Radius);

    // The distance to the circle: negative inside the disk.
    ToSdf(c: Circle): FunctionSdf2D
        => FunctionSdf2D(p => c.Center.Between(p).Magnitude - c.Radius);

    // The distance to the capsule's surface: negative inside the swept solid.
    ToSdf(c: Capsule3D): FunctionSdf3D
        => FunctionSdf3D(p => DistanceToCapsule(p, c.A, c.B, c.Radius));

    // The planar form: negative inside the stadium.
    ToSdf(c: Capsule2D): FunctionSdf2D
        => FunctionSdf2D(p => DistanceToCapsule(p, c.A, c.B, c.Radius));

    // The distance to the annulus: negative between the two circles, positive both
    // inside the hole and outside the outer rim.
    ToSdf(a: Annulus): FunctionSdf2D
        => FunctionSdf2D(p =>
            (a.Center.Between(p).Magnitude - (a.InnerRadius + a.OuterRadius) * 0.5).Abs
            - (a.OuterRadius - a.InnerRadius) * 0.5);

    // The plane as the field of the half-space BEHIND it: negative on the back side,
    // positive on the side Normal points to. A plane has no thickness, so this is
    // the only reading of it that carries a sign; take `.Abs` of the result for the
    // unsigned distance to the plane itself.
    ToSdf(pl: Plane): FunctionSdf3D
        => FunctionSdf3D(p => pl.SignedDistance(p));

    // The half-space's own field: negative inside it, which is the same field as its
    // boundary plane's, stated on the type that actually denotes the solid region.
    ToSdf(h: HalfSpace): FunctionSdf3D
        => FunctionSdf3D(p => h.Boundary.SignedDistance(p));

    // The planar counterpart: negative inside the half-plane.
    ToSdf(h: HalfPlane2D): FunctionSdf2D
        => FunctionSdf2D(p => h.SignedDistance(p));

    // The distance to the segment. Zero-thickness: non-negative everywhere, zero
    // only on the segment.
    ToSdf(l: Line2D): FunctionSdf2D
        => FunctionSdf2D(p => DistanceToSegment(l.A, l.B, p));

    // The segment thickened by radius — a stadium, and a true signed field.
    // Equivalent to `Capsule2D(l.A, l.B, radius).ToSdf`.
    ToSdf(l: Line2D, radius: Number): FunctionSdf2D
        => FunctionSdf2D(p => DistanceToCapsule(p, l.A, l.B, radius));

    // The distance to the segment in space. Zero-thickness, as in the plane.
    ToSdf(l: Line3D): FunctionSdf3D
        => FunctionSdf3D(p => DistanceToSegment(l.A, l.B, p));

    // The segment thickened by radius — a capsule, and a true signed field.
    ToSdf(l: Line3D, radius: Number): FunctionSdf3D
        => FunctionSdf3D(p => DistanceToCapsule(p, l.A, l.B, radius));

    // The triangle in the plane is a SOLID region, so this is a true signed field:
    // negative inside. Winding-agnostic, following DistanceToTriangle.
    ToSdf(t: Triangle2D): FunctionSdf2D
        => FunctionSdf2D(p => DistanceToTriangle(p, t.A, t.B, t.C));

    // The quadrilateral in the plane, likewise solid and signed. Concave rings are
    // handled; the ring must be simple. Precondition: as DistanceToQuad.
    ToSdf(q: Quad2D): FunctionSdf2D
        => FunctionSdf2D(p => DistanceToQuad(p, q.A, q.B, q.C, q.D));

    // The triangle in SPACE is a patch, not a solid: zero-thickness, so the field is
    // non-negative and zero only on the patch. This is the per-face building block a
    // mesh-to-field conversion would take the minimum over — with the caveat that
    // the minimum of unsigned face fields is itself unsigned, and recovering a sign
    // for a closed mesh needs a separate inside test.
    ToSdf(t: Triangle3D): FunctionSdf3D
        => FunctionSdf3D(p => UnsignedDistanceToTriangle(p, t.A, t.B, t.C));

    // The triangle patch given a thickness: the plate of all points within half of
    // thickness of it, with rounded edges and rim. A true signed field.
    ToSdf(t: Triangle3D, thickness: Number): FunctionSdf3D
        => FunctionSdf3D(p =>
            UnsignedDistanceToTriangle(p, t.A, t.B, t.C) - thickness * 0.5);

    // The quad patch in space: zero-thickness, as the triangle. Exact for a planar
    // quad; see UnsignedDistanceToQuad for the non-planar caveat.
    ToSdf(q: Quad3D): FunctionSdf3D
        => FunctionSdf3D(p => UnsignedDistanceToQuad(p, q.A, q.B, q.C, q.D));

    // The quad patch thickened into a rounded plate. A true signed field.
    ToSdf(q: Quad3D, thickness: Number): FunctionSdf3D
        => FunctionSdf3D(p =>
            UnsignedDistanceToQuad(p, q.A, q.B, q.C, q.D) - thickness * 0.5);

    //==
    // # Time-varying field bodies
    //
    // Bodies for the time-varying field interfaces declared in
    // `fields.concepts.plato`: sampling at an instant, and the change
    // and monotonicity queries between two instants.

    //==
    // # ITimeVaryingScalarField2D
    //
    // A planar scalar field evolving over a timeline; sampled at (point, time).
    // TODO(interface-gap): an average rate of change would divide the value change
    // by the elapsed time, but Instant differences yield a Duration and no
    // sanctioned Duration-to-Number division is in scope here; only the raw
    // change and monotonicity tests are offered.

    // The scalar value at the point at a given instant; a readable spelling of
    // EvalAtTime.
    ValueAtTime(self: ITimeVaryingScalarField2D, point: Point2D, time: Instant): Number
        => self.EvalAtTime(point, time);
